My land is about 8 mu — what my family has worked for decades. I don't think about changing much. My husband handles the heavier labor but mostly it falls to me now. Everyone in the village grows wheat in winter and corn in summer on the same land. That's what I know, that's what my mother did, that's what makes sense.

I'll plant wheat come October on all 8 mu. I buy seeds from the village seed shop — last year it was a common improved variety, I don't remember the name, I just ask for what works here. I apply the bag fertilizer at planting — compound stuff — then add urea when the wheat starts jointing in spring. I water 3 times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once when it heads out. I spray twice — once for weeds in early spring, once for bugs when the aphids come. I use the rotary tiller after the corn harvest to prepare the soil.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn immediately on the same ground — hybrid seeds, everyone uses those now, the yield is better. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when it's knee-high. I only water if it looks dry at tasseling — the summer rains usually help. One pesticide spray if the corn borer shows up.

I expect about 420 jin per mu for wheat, maybe 550 for corn. Nothing fancy. It pays the bills.
